housing: Rother has one of the oldest populations in England, and Bexhill-on-Sea is its main town, with Edwardian and Victorian seafront villas and terraces (many converted into flats) and large areas of bungalows. Rye and Battle are historic towns with listed timber-framed and Georgian houses, while the High Weald villages have weatherboarded and tile-hung cottages and country houses, often off the gas grid. Along the coast at Camber and Winchelsea Beach there are bungalows and holiday homes. Private renting is a modest share of homes.
checkinTips: Converted seafront flats in Bexhill: record communal hallways, meter cupboards, fire doors and salt marks or rust on windows and railings.
Bungalows across Bexhill and Little Common: photograph loft hatches, flat-roof extensions, gardens and any adaptations such as grab rails.
Listed timber-framed houses in Rye and Battle: photograph beams, uneven floors, old windows and damp, and note what the tenant must not alter.
Weald cottages: photograph oil tanks with the fuel level, stoves, chimneys and any septic tank or private drainage.
Coastal homes at Camber, Winchelsea Beach and Fairlight: record sand and salt wear, exposed walls and signs of flooding or cliff-top weathering.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Rother District Council's environmental health team.
